# MAVI Offline Binary Kit

This directory defines the **companion binary kit** kept separately from ordinary Git history.

The source repository carries scripts, policies, version catalogs and manifests. Large third-party installers/runtime payloads and generated dependency caches live in a separately retained binary kit so that:

- ordinary Git clones stay small;
- third-party executables cannot enter source history accidentally;
- every external payload is SHA-256 bound before use;
- licence/notices and exact observed versions travel with the retained kit;
- the same approved kit can prepare multiple disconnected Development workstations and can feed Production setup-media assembly.

## Recommended storage

Keep the extracted folder beside the repository:

~~~text
<workspace>/
  MAVI/
  MAVI-Offline-Binary-Kit/
~~~

The repository Development launcher auto-detects this sibling folder when its manifest is present.

The kit generated by `tools/setup/New-MaviOfflineBinaryKit.ps1` has this layout:

~~~text
MAVI-Offline-Binary-Kit/
  README-FIRST.txt
  mavi-offline-binary-kit.json
  catalog/
    offline-binary-catalog-v1.json
  vendor/
    ffmpeg/
      manifest.json
      win-x64/
        ffmpeg.exe
        ffprobe.exe
        LICENSE.txt
    postgresql/
      pg18/
        win-x64/
          manifest.json
          LICENSE-POSTGRESQL.txt
          LICENSE-PGVECTOR.txt
          bin/
          lib/
          share/
    installers/
      win-x64/
        dotnet-hosting.exe
        dotnet-sdk.exe
        node.msi
        python.exe
    developer-cache/
      win-x64/
        nuget-packages/
        npm-cache/
        python-wheelhouse/
~~~

## What belongs in Git

Keep these in ordinary Git:

- source code;
- setup/build/verification scripts;
- JSON schemas/configuration;
- dependency/version policy;
- text licences/notices that belong to repository-owned material;
- hash manifests and release metadata when they do not embed the large payload itself.

Do **not** put third-party EXE/DLL/MSI/ZIP/7z/WHL/SO/PYD payloads, model weights, generated caches or large runtime packs into ordinary Git merely because an individual file happens to be small.

The binary kit is the controlled home for those payloads.

## Version record

`config/dependencies/offline-binary-catalog-v1.json` records the repository-approved baseline and version policy.

The generated `mavi-offline-binary-kit.json` records the exact SHA-256 and size of every retained file, the observed PostgreSQL/pgvector/FFmpeg versions, and exact installer metadata for the ASP.NET Hosting Bundle, .NET SDK, Node MSI and Python installer. Toolchain installers are therefore identified by both readable version metadata and cryptographic file identity, then revalidated after installation.

The final MAVI setup bundle has its own manifest, so provenance is chained:

~~~text
repository policy/catalog
        ↓
offline binary kit manifest
        ↓
application artifact + setup-bundle manifest
        ↓
disconnected qualification evidence
~~~

## Vision runtime

CPU/CUDA model/runtime bundles remain separately qualified because their validity is hardware/platform specific. Keep them with the same release archive, but do not treat the Windows application binary kit as a substitute for Task-17 vision-runtime qualification.
